coverage_limits: OpenAlex's shared anonymous budget ran out early in the run, so citation chasing used Semantic Scholar, which lacks some citing works (the NBER version of the cybernetic teammate paper returned 404). ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis, Wiley, SSRN, and the Oulu repository returned 403. Some abstracts therefore come from Semantic Scholar or search snippets, and four 2026 records (Zhang & Xia, Mascareno et al., Serin & Kepceoglu, Schmidt et al.) are listed on title and Crossref metadata only. ProQuest could not be searched directly; dissertations were covered through Crossref's dissertation type and web search. No registered report and no multi-site study on generative AI and creativity was found beyond the multi-country Ashkinaze et al. experiment (already collected) and the Chinese-language arm of the Epitome replication. No replication or published comment was found for Doshi & Hauser apart from Epitome, nor for Padmakumar & He, Anderson et al., or Dell'Acqua et al. Haslberger, Gingrich and Bhatia (SSRN 4594466), a UK extension of Noy & Zhang, was checked and left out because its tasks have no creativity or originality outcome. Education quasi-experiments with Torrance tests that surfaced in web search were not followed up because they fall outside this lane. The sample size of the Epitome Doshi-Hauser replication is not stated in the main text.

candidates.title: Reply to: ChatGPT decreases idea diversity in brainstorming
candidates.task: reply to a group-level re-analysis of brainstorming data
candidates.evidence: Authors' reply to Meincke, Nave and Terwiesch (2025), who re-analysed the public data of Lee and Chung (2024) at the group level and found lower idea diversity in pooled ChatGPT-assisted responses. The publisher page indicates the reply contrasts individual creativity with collective diversity and reports no new data.

candidates.title: A comment on "An Empirical Investigation of the Impact of ChatGPT on Creativity"
candidates.venue: I4R Discussion Paper Series No. 274 (Institute for Replication, EconStor)
other_versions: OSF project https://osf.io/nk6ev (Institute for Replication; file Replication_Report_1.pdf and code Codes_Coitaetal.zip)
candidates.task: computational reproduction of ChatGPT vs web-search vs no-assistance idea-generation experiments
candidates.evidence: Reproduction of Lee and Chung (2024) from the original data and code. All main results reproduced, with two minor coding errors and one table typo that do not change conclusions. A new robustness check on Experiment 3 found no link between response time and rated creativity in the ChatGPT condition (r = -.079).

candidates.title: Replication Report on “An empirical investigation of the impact of ChatGPT on creativity”
other_versions: OSF project https://osf.io/nk6ev (Institute for Replication; file Reproduction_Report_Woods.pdf)
candidates.task: reproduction and robustness checks of ChatGPT-assisted idea-generation experiments
candidates.evidence: Reproduces Lee and Chung (2024) in R and Stata. Results hold when ratings are analysed one by one or by principal components, with ChatGPT ratings in place of human ratings, and under stricter exclusions. The report notes ChatGPT may not raise practical or useful ratings in some experiments.

candidates.title: Epitome: Pioneering an Experimental Platform for AI-Social Science Integration
candidates.task: short adventure story writing with zero, one, or five AI ideas, in English and Chinese
candidates.evidence: Platform paper that replicates Doshi and Hauser (2024). Participants were randomly assigned to human-only, one AI idea, or five AI ideas, and experts rated writing quality, content quality and originality. Rated creativity rose (42.1 percent with one idea, 16.4 percent with five) while collective diversity fell by 5.6 to 6.5 percent, in both languages. The paper also replicates Noy and Zhang with 46 managers. The story-task sample size is not stated in the main text.

candidates.title: The creative musical achievement of AI systems compared to music students: A replication of the study by Schreiber et al. (2024)
other_versions: OSF Preprints 2025-07-06 (author order Schreiber, Kopiez, Meier, Sander)
candidates.task: melody continuation by LLMs versus human composers
candidates.evidence: Replication of Schreiber et al. (2024). 75 melodic continuations from Qwen 2, Llama 3 and ChatGPT-4 were compared with 23 human solutions. 54 music-student listeners rated them, and human solutions beat all three AI systems on every criterion (d_z 1.11 to 2.51). The 54 participants are raters.

candidates.title: Time-on-task and instructions help humans to keep up with AI: replication and extension of a comparison of creative performances
candidates.task: Alternate Uses Task and Remote Associates Task, humans versus AI chatbots
candidates.evidence: Replicates an earlier human-versus-AI comparison on the Alternate Uses Task and extends it with instructions that ask for quality and quantity, more time for humans, and the Remote Associates Task. AI mean scores stayed higher, but maximum scores did not differ in the modified condition. The human sample size is not in the abstract.

candidates.title: How Strong Is the Evidence for the Artificial Hivemind? Reevaluating Evidence for the Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models
candidates.task: re-analysis of open-ended LLM response homogeneity
candidates.evidence: Re-analysis of a prior paper's claim that LLM open-ended answers converge. Under stricter null comparisons, much of the measured homogeneity reflects answering the same prompt, and prompting raises measured diversity. Model outputs only, with no human data, so likely context at most. Included as a re-analysis in the homogenization literature.

candidates.title: Are LLMs becoming similarly creative? Evidence from three years of models
candidates.task: LLM answers to open-ended user queries and the Alternate Uses Task across model releases
candidates.evidence: Follow-up to the cross-model homogeneity work of Wenger and Kenett (2025, already collected). Sentence-embedding similarity of model outputs across three years of releases shows output diversity falling over time. Model outputs only, with no human participants.

candidates.title: Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 European Conference on Cognitive Ergonomics, 198-201
candidates.task: meta-analysis of homogenization in human-AI co-creation
candidates.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies (61 effect sizes) that finds a small homogenization effect of AI use (d = 0.334), robust to sensitivity checks and publication bias. It may be a short conference version of the same authors' Behaviour & Information Technology meta-analysis, which is already collected.

candidates.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
candidates.task: occupation-specific incentivized professional writing tasks
candidates.evidence: Preregistered online experiment in which 453 college-educated professionals did writing tasks and half were randomly exposed to ChatGPT. Evaluators gave an overall grade and separate grades for writing quality, content quality and originality. Per the working paper, grades rose about 0.45 SD, with similar gains on the originality sub-grade.

candidates.title: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation
candidates.venue: SSRN working paper; Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Department of Economics Working Paper No. 16/WP/2026
other_versions: Replication package: Figshare doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.32132980; Mendeley Data doi 10.17632/t93pf5r6fp
candidates.task: short open-ended creative writing text (about 150 words) in the lab
candidates.evidence: Lab experiment with 360 participants at VERALabEx in a 2x3 design. Participants were randomly assigned to ChatGPT access or no AI, crossed with incentive schemes, and independent Prolific evaluators scored creative performance. AI access raised scores only through active use, with a concave relation to the number of queries.

candidates.title: Generative AI Enhances Team Performance and Reduces Need for Traditional Teams
candidates.task: team content-creation and innovation/strategy tasks
candidates.evidence: Randomized experiment with 435 participants in 122 teams, plus a second experiment with individuals, comparing teams and individuals with and without generative AI. Blind online judges rated outputs on overall quality, novelty and usefulness, and AI-augmented teams outperformed human-only teams.

candidates.title: Generative AI Does Not Erase Individual Differences in Human Creativity
candidates.task: story writing and idea generation with GPT-4o
candidates.evidence: Two studies (N = 442) in which all participants worked with an LLM. Baseline creative ability and intelligence predicted the originality of AI-assisted output, and the authors identify an AI-assisted creativity factor separate from unassisted creativity. There is no random assignment to AI versus no AI.

candidates.title: One Tool, One Taste? How Vibe Coding Trades Collective Diversity for Individual Creativity
candidates.task: promotional websites built with the Lovable vibe-coding tool in a graded course
candidates.evidence: Analyses 73 homepages built by graduate students with Lovable under an assignment that rewarded original design. DINOv3 embeddings show high pairwise similarity and most sites in a few clusters. There is no non-AI comparison group.

candidates.title: Assimilating generative AI into ideation work: seeding, search and human contribution
candidates.task: ideation by professionals under four human-GenAI configurations
candidates.evidence: Tests four configurations with 400 professionals: human-only ideation, unstructured human-GenAI collaboration, GenAI seeding, and a TC-based GenAI configuration. Experts rated novelty, utility and feasibility. Only the TC-based configuration raised novelty relative to the other GenAI conditions. The abstract does not state random assignment.

candidates.title: Floor Raiser or Ceiling Limiter? Differential Storytelling Outcomes with a Child-Centric GenAI System Across Individual Differences
candidates.task: children's storytelling with a GenAI system versus a traditional storyboard
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects experiment with 40 children aged 7 to 12 that compares GenAI-assisted and traditional storyboard conditions. The GenAI condition improved rated creativity and richness and narrowed the quality gap between children.

candidates.title: Reviving Reflection-in-Action: Instilling Designerly Thinking in AI-Supported Ideation through Multimodal Prompting
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition, 359-376
candidates.task: design ideation with an AI creativity support tool prompted by text, sketch, or sketch plus tags
candidates.evidence: Within-participants study with design students comparing input modalities for a prototype AI tool (SketchifAI). Divergent thinking was scored for fluency, variety, originality and quality. Sketch input tended to raise fluency, with inconclusive differences in originality. There is no no-AI arm, only AI-configuration variants.

candidates.title: "Like Taking the Path of Least Resistance": Exploring the Impact of LLM Interaction on the Creative Process of Programming
candidates.task: programming problems solved with and without an LLM
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study with 20 programmers in LLM-assisted and unassisted conditions. LLM use shortened idea generation and reduced creative moments. LLM-assisted solutions contained about the same number of ideas as unassisted ones.

candidates.title: How Creative Is AI Writing? Generative and Collaborative AI in Japanese Fiction
candidates.task: story endings by human authors, zero-shot AI, detailed-prompt AI, and human-AI collaboration
candidates.evidence: 58 readers with creative-writing backgrounds ranked endings of 25 Japanese stories across four authorship conditions on quality and originality. Human-AI collaboration ranked highest on quality but lowest on originality. The 58 participants are raters.

candidates.title: AI-AI co-creation outperforms human pairs in creative tasks
candidates.task: three open-ended ideation tasks: AI-AI pairs, single AI, human pairs
candidates.evidence: Compares two AI-AI co-creation setups, single-AI creation and human-human pairs. Trained judges rated 1,212 ideas on creativity, novelty and usefulness. AI-AI co-creation scored highest on creativity and novelty, and human pairs scored lowest. The number of human participants is not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Does AI Homogenize Student Thinking? A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Structural Convergence in AI-Augmented Essays
candidates.task: student essays from the AIDE Kaggle corpus rewritten by an LLM under three prompt strategies
candidates.evidence: Analyses 6,875 essays across human-only, AI-only and three human-plus-AI conditions. Quality rose while the structural diversity of essays fell on some dimensions. The human-plus-AI essays are LLM rewrites of existing human essays, so no person received AI help.

candidates.title: "Looking for Something Weird to Happen": How Humans Sustain AI Agent Novelty Amid Semantic Collapse
candidates.authors: Lai, Woemmel, Mao, Kim, Ann, Evans
candidates.task: user-configured AI agents on the MOLTBOOK social network
candidates.evidence: Output of 30,076 user-steered AI agents grew less diverse within agents and more similar across agents over weeks. Interviews (N = 11) and a survey (N = 53) link sustained novelty to users who supply distinctive material. Borderline, because the outputs are agents' outputs.

candidates.title: Humans Introduce, Models Elaborate: Asymmetric Narrative Agency in Human-LLM Co-Writing
candidates.task: turn-based collaborative storytelling: human-human, human-LLM, LLM-LLM
candidates.evidence: Compares matched human-human, human-LLM and LLM-LLM storytelling with turn-level measures of semantic novelty, transience and resonance. Humans introduce more novel material, and LLMs elaborate the existing context.

candidates.title: How Did Writing Change At CHI? Analyzing 44 Years of CHI Writing Before and After the Introduction of Large Language Models
candidates.task: full texts of 14,262 CHI papers, 1982-2026
candidates.evidence: Measures readability, register, lexical diversity and LLM marker words across 44 years of CHI papers. Prose did not homogenize after LLMs and vocabulary grew more varied, with LLMs speeding up a shift that began earlier.

candidates.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Monoculture: AI Homogenizes Syntax, Not (Necessarily) Semantics
other_versions: arXiv 2607.13077v1 titled The Hitchhiker's Guide to Monoculture
candidates.task: Kaggle competition code submissions, 2019 to mid-2026
candidates.evidence: Within-contest similarity of Kaggle submissions rose in surface syntax (TF-IDF) but not in approach or intent (code embeddings), alongside convergence on the random seed 42.

candidates.title: AI-Associated Lexical Shifts Across 34 Languages: Cross-Lingual Convergence and Diachronic Uptake in News Writing
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (committed to EMNLP 2026 per arXiv comment)
candidates.task: news writing in 34 languages (WMT News Crawl)
candidates.evidence: AI-overused words rose after ChatGPT's release in 26 of 34 languages, with cross-lingual convergence on related concepts. The outcome is lexical convergence, a homogenization proxy rather than a creativity rating.

candidates.title: Divergent creativity in humans and large language models
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task and creative writing (haiku, synopses, flash fiction)
candidates.evidence: Benchmarks LLM semantic divergence against a dataset of 100,000 humans. LLMs can beat average human DAT scores but stay below the more creative half of humans.

candidates.title: Unraveling Creativity Through Variability: A Comparison of LLMs and Humans in an Educational Q&A Scenario
candidates.task: answers to children's questions in early-childhood education style
candidates.evidence: Compares semantic and syntactic diversity of LLM answers with a large human-authored dataset. LLM outputs vary less than human answers, especially on repeated questions.

candidates.title: The paradox of creativity in generative AI: high performance, human-like bias, and limited differential evaluation
candidates.task: egg task (divergent thinking)
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4o (12 runs) versus 47 human participants, plus pooled data from eight prior studies, on fluency, category diversity and fixation. ChatGPT produced more ideas but showed similar fixation on conventional categories.

candidates.title: Are Semantic Networks Associated with Idea Originality in Artificial Creativity? A Comparison with Human Agents
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-18
candidates.task: standardized creativity tests and semantic network measures, ChatGPT-4o versus psychology students
candidates.evidence: Gives the same tests to ChatGPT-4o and 81 psychology students split into higher and lower creative groups. ChatGPT-4o had a more rigid semantic network but was more original than the lower creative humans.

candidates.title: Assessment of the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Creative Storytelling for Enhancing the Ideation Process at the Individual Level
candidates.venue: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Creative Technologies 11
candidates.task: Guilford Alternative Uses Test and creative storytelling
candidates.evidence: Ten polytechnic students were split into two groups, and one group worked with ChatGPT. ChatGPT raised fluency, flexibility and originality on the Alternative Uses Test but not in the storytelling task. Very small sample, and assignment method not stated.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.task: creative writing with an interactive AI assistant
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered RCT in which participants could use AI. Those rewarded for originality relative to peers wrote collectively more diverse texts than those rewarded for quality, and they copied fewer AI suggestions verbatim. The randomized factor is the incentive scheme, and all participants had AI access.

candidates.title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
candidates.task: NLP researchers executing randomly assigned LLM-generated or expert-written research ideas
candidates.evidence: Follow-up to Si et al.'s ideation study, which is already collected. 43 expert researchers executed randomly assigned ideas written by experts or generated by an LLM, and blind reviewers scored novelty, excitement, effectiveness and overall quality. LLM ideas lost more score after execution, closing or reversing the earlier advantage.

candidates.title: The Basic B*** Effect: The Use of LLM-based Agents Reduces the Distinctiveness and Diversity of People's Choices
candidates.task: choices made by LLM agents versus people (social media behavior; movie choices)
candidates.evidence: Compares choices by generic and personalized LLM agents with human choices, using 1,000 social media users in Study 1 and 348 experiment participants in Study 2. Agents reduced the distinctiveness and diversity of choices. The outcome is choice homogenization, not creative output.

candidates.title: “Who” Is the Best Creative Thinking Partner? An Experimental Investigation of Human–Human, Human–Internet, and Human–AI Co‐Creation
candidates.venue: The Journal of Creative Behavior 59(3), e1519
candidates.task: alternate uses, consequences, and problem-solving tasks in dyads, with the internet, or with AI
candidates.evidence: Between-group experiment with 202 German participants in four conditions: human-human dyads, human-internet, and two human-AI conditions with basic or specific instructions. Human dyads scored higher on divergent thinking, with no group differences on problem solving. The abstract does not state random assignment.

candidates.title: Using AI to Generate Visual Art: Do Individual Differences in Creativity Predict AI-Assisted Art Quality?
candidates.task: wordsets fed to DALL-E to generate images, rated for creativity
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered online study in which participants' divergent thinking (AUT, DAT) and the semantic diversity of their wordsets predicted the rated creativity of the DALL-E images, with modest effects. There is no no-AI comparison.

candidates.title: When ChatGPT Writes Your Research Proposal: Scientific Creativity in the Age of Generative AI
candidates.task: short research proposal for a fictitious experimental psychology scenario
candidates.evidence: Graduate students wrote, and ChatGPT-4 generated, brief research proposals that two experts rated blind for scientific creativity. ChatGPT scored higher overall and on originality and meaningfulness. The student sample size is not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Does ChatGPT know what robots are thinking? - Evaluation of human-created vs. AI-generated scientific ideas
candidates.authors: Eymann, Lachmann, Hekele, Ashok, Berns, Czernochowski
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Annual Conference of the European Association of Cognitive Ergonomics, 1-5
candidates.task: short research proposal for a robotics scenario
candidates.evidence: Graduate students' and ChatGPT's research proposals were rated by two scientists. ChatGPT scored higher overall, but the two raters disagreed strongly on originality.

candidates.title: Empowering Engineering Students Through Artificial Intelligence (AI): Blended Human–AI Creative Ideation Processes With ChatGPT
candidates.venue: Computer Applications in Engineering Education 33(1), e22817
candidates.task: engineering ideation by third-year students (728 ideas)
candidates.evidence: Randomized controlled experiment with third-year engineering students plus a survey. There were no significant differences in ideation outcomes between AI and no-AI groups, but prior ChatGPT experience mattered. This differs from the same first author's crossover study, which is already collected.

candidates.title: Design Requirements for Responsible AI Tools in Education: Empirical Study on ChatGPT and Creative Thinking
candidates.venue: 2025 IEEE 33rd International Requirements Engineering Conference Workshops (REW), 448-452
candidates.task: creative thinking tasks among undergraduates
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment (N = 60) plus a survey (N = 100). ChatGPT raised idea fluency but not originality or flexibility. Assignment method not stated.

candidates.title: Comparative Study of Generative AI and Traditional Tools for Evaluating Creativity and Efficiency in UI/UX Desig
candidates.venue: International Journal of Innovations in Science and Technology, 924
candidates.task: UI/UX design with Galileo AI versus Figma, novice and expert designers
candidates.evidence: Experiment comparing a generative AI design tool with a traditional tool. Creativity was rated with the Creative Product Semantic Scale, and the traditional tool scored higher on creativity while AI cut cognitive load and time. The registered title appears truncated ("Desig").

candidates.title: How and For Whom Using Generative AI Affects Creativity: A Field Experiment
candidates.task: employees' work at a technology consulting firm
candidates.evidence: Field experiment in which employees were randomly assigned to LLM assistance or not. Supervisors and external evaluators rated creativity, and LLM assistance raised it, more so for employees high in metacognitive strategies. Sample size not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Help That Hurts: The Creativity Cost of Generative AI Ideation in Music Composition
candidates.task: composing an original 15-second piano melody
candidates.evidence: RCT in which musically trained participants were assigned to an AI-ideation group or a no-AI control. External listeners rated AI-condition melodies as less creative, and AI access changed stylistic choices. Sample size not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a cognitive support tool in early-stage design ideation: A human–AI co-ideation experiment
candidates.task: early-stage design ideation with a text-and-image AI workflow versus human-only brainstorming
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment with 32 design students and expert ratings on six criteria. AI-assisted outputs scored higher on problem framing, while human-only outputs scored higher on innovation and solution strategies.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Creativity
candidates.venue: Master of Science thesis, School of Psychology, Te Herenga Waka - Victoria University of Wellington
candidates.task: brainstorming (originality, flexibility, fluency, elaboration) and the Divergent Association Task
candidates.evidence: MSc thesis with two experiments comparing generative-AI groups with a non-AI group. In the first, AI use raised all four brainstorming scores. In the second, groups differed in originality but not in semantic distance or heart-rate measures. Assignment method and sample size not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Effects of Human-AI Collaboration in the Ideation Stage of the Design Process
candidates.venue: Master of Human-Computer Interaction thesis, Carleton University
candidates.task: website sketches with AI-generated inspiration, search-engine inspiration, or none
candidates.evidence: Thesis experiment comparing AI-generated inspiration, search-engine inspiration and no inspiration, with design performance, eye tracking and trust measures. AI inspiration increased design fixation compared with search. Assignment method and sample size not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Two Studies on Assessing AI-Augmented Creativity with Large Language Models
candidates.venue: PhD dissertation, Michigan State University (Business Administration - Information Technology Management)
candidates.task: creative work with LLMs set to different randomness levels, rated by evaluators
candidates.evidence: Study 1 is a quasi-experiment on how LLM randomness affects perceived creativity of work. High-randomness suggestions did not raise rated creativity. Study 2 is on AI-text detection. Design details and sample size not on the record page.

candidates.title: Creativity in the AI era
candidates.venue: PhD thesis (Doctorat en psychologie), Université Paris Cité
candidates.task: EPoC creativity test given to 100 ChatGPT instances; survey of 301 people on perceptions of GenAI
candidates.evidence: Thesis of four articles. The experimental article tests 100 ChatGPT runs on EPoC and finds high idea production but lower diversity and flexibility. The other empirical article is a perception survey. There is no human-AI assistance experiment, so it is likely out of scope.

candidates.title: The impact of generative AI on design ideation : exploring the influence of AI-generated stimuli and design fixation
candidates.venue: University of Oulu thesis (degree level not confirmed)
candidates.task: design exercises comparing human-only ideation, online image search, and GenAI tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney)
candidates.evidence: Per search snippets, 18 students in a Human and AI Creativity course did structured design exercises with and without GenAI, and the thesis examines creative performance and design fixation. The repository page returned 403, so year, degree and design are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: A New Muse: How Guided AI Use Impacts Creativity in Online Creative Writing Courses
candidates.venue: Oregon State Ecampus Research Unit, Research Fellows white paper (April 2025)
candidates.task: creative writing exercise in online introductory fiction courses
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study with 31 students writing in three conditions: no ChatGPT, ChatGPT alone, and ChatGPT with instructor guidance. Expert judges scored creativity with the Consensual Assessment Technique. ChatGPT alone did not change creativity, while guided use raised it, mainly for low-baseline students.

candidates.title: The creativity of artificial intelligence
candidates.venue: Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics 121, 102528
other_versions: Mendeley Data replication package, The Creativity of AI - Replication, doi 10.17632/vt8tg8tvrs (2026)
candidates.task: creativity ratings and auction bids for human-made versus Stable Diffusion artworks
candidates.evidence: Per search snippets, participants rated the creativity of commissioned human artworks and Stable Diffusion versions in three styles and bid for them in auctions. AI landscapes were rated more creative. It is unclear whether raters knew the source, so this may be a perception study. The replication package mentions Singapore, US, Japan and Korea data, which suggests a multi-country design.

candidates.title: Creative minds in the age of AI. personality traits, AI perception, and creativity tasks
candidates.venue: Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics 125, 102659
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task, Alternate Uses Task and a constrained narrative task done without AI, plus an AI-use questionnaire
candidates.evidence: 260 participants reported AI use and attitudes and completed unassisted creativity tasks. Creativity was highest with moderate, reflective AI use and lower with minimal or heavy reliance. The design is correlational, with no AI during the tasks.
